fixed_constraints: Complete macos-15 candidate gates operate PostgreSQL 17, Node 24 plus pinned Playwright Chromium, the pinned Bun archive, and TypeScript 7.0.2; release uploads, credentialed signing, and live provider calls remain out of scope.

Unnarrowed execution covers go tests everywhere, 850 bun runtime tests, cataloguegen, modcheck, gramcheck, gofmt, vet, and strict tsc over fresh emit, with a fully serviced local run reporting zero skips.
Committed-golden tscheck files vanished in I44, so the TypeScript gate must be recreated for fresh emit rather than adjusted from golden includes.
Required services each gain a setup script or command, pins each gain a committed lockfile or target record, and genuine no-run rows each gain a written justification.
common.purpose: Determine the three open I45 design points for Can gating: CI topology, the mechanism carrying fresh emit into TypeScript, and the TS gate evidence level.

emit_evidence.background: CI TypeScript gating over fresh emit can end at the job log or continue into persisted artifacts holding the tree and the tsc log.
facts: Existing workflows already upload test logs, qualification reports, and integrity records, which normalizes artifact upload as gate practice.
A retained tree preserves the precise bytes tsc checked for later audit, while log-only evidence expires with the run log.
Each push and pull request pays storage and upload minutes for artifacts, against zero marginal cost for log streaming.

gate_topology.background: Go, bun, live service legs, mirrors, and fresh-emit tsc all need macos-15 coverage, either within an extended single job or split across operated gates.
facts: The current verifier job covers a go test subset with only Bun operated, so database, browser, and strict-TS coverage skip silently in CI today.
macos-15 lacks docker, leaving brew services for PostgreSQL, npm plus pinned Playwright for Chromium, and a committed lockfile for tsc.
Shared setup with a unified verdict favors one job; per-family failure isolation favors split gates with repeated setup and files.

tscheck_mechanism.background: A reviewable, locally runnable step must turn the eight maintained examples into a fresh emit tree for strict tsc.
facts: Staged stdlib coverage already asserts and builds each project twice identically, so an env-gated copy adds about ten lines on the proven path.
Standing up another Go emitter duplicates staging and bundle logic beside tested code, inviting divergence between suite and gate.
Running ahead of tsc in the same job from the same archive, both routes agree whenever shared build logic agrees.
